uncited: Billboard Voxelization is a two-pass rasterization-based technique that initializes a position map by rendering instanced quads (billboards) corresponding to voxel centers, writing the nearest world-space positions to a framebuffer.

It differs from [Position Map Voxelization](2604-position-map-voxelization.md) by explicitly rendering geometry to establish depth, and from [Hardware-accelerated surface voxelization via 2D textures](4042-hardware-accelerated-surface-voxelization-via-2d-textures.md) by using a full position map rather than just depth or surface normals.

Creates a Framebuffer Object (FBO) with a color attachment (position map) and a depth attachment for voxelization rendering.
The color attachment is a 2D texture with internal format `GL_RGBA32F`, width and height matching window dimensions, nearest filtering, and clamp to edge wrapping.
-   **Time Complexity:** $O(N)$ where $N$ is the number of voxels, as each voxel is rendered as a billboard.
-   **Memory Complexity:** $O(W \cdot H)$ for the position map and depth buffer, plus $O(N)$ for the instance data.
High-resolution volumes and large windows increase memory bandwidth usage.
-   **Strengths:** Simple to implement using standard graphics APIs; handles arbitrary voxel shapes via billboard geometry; provides a full position map for subsequent ray marching.

-   **Limitations:** Requires rendering all voxels, which can be slow for very high-resolution volumes; depth fighting may occur if voxels are coplanar or very close; requires careful handling of the position reconstruction in the fragment shader.
-   **When to use:** When a full position map is needed for advanced volume rendering techniques (e.g., ray marching with position-based shading) and the volume resolution is moderate.
-   **When not to use:** For very high-resolution volumes where performance is critical, or when only a depth map is sufficient.
